questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Loops with @each” in Dart Sass?
options: The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.

Control-flow rules turn structured Sass values into a predictable set of CSS rules. Choose `@if` for decisions and `@each`, `@for`, or `@while` for iteration when it makes the generated output clearer than writing each rule manually.
questions.answer_key: Control-flow rules turn structured Sass values into a predictable set of CSS rules. Choose `@if` for decisions and `@each`, `@for`, or `@while` for iteration when it makes the generated output clearer than writing each rule manually.
questions.explanation: Control-flow rules turn structured Sass values into a predictable set of CSS rules. Choose `@if` for decisions and `@each`, `@for`, or `@while` for iteration when it makes the generated output clearer than writing each rule manually. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Iterating over lists”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
Identify the collection, the per-item rule, and the stopping condition. Validate collection shape and inspect the count and naming of generated rules.
Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
questions.answer_key: Identify the collection, the per-item rule, and the stopping condition. Validate collection shape and inspect the count and naming of generated rules.
questions.explanation: Identify the collection, the per-item rule, and the stopping condition. Validate collection shape and inspect the count and naming of generated rules. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

questions.prompt: Which review decision most directly supports maintainability for “Loops with @each”?
options: Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.

Bound the data you iterate over, validate configuration before generating selectors, and inspect both selector names and output size. Generated CSS is a public interface that other components and developers may depend on.
Generate every possible selector or theme combination, even when most variants are never used.
Treat successful compilation as proof that the interface is accessible and behaves correctly in every browser.
questions.answer_key: Bound the data you iterate over, validate configuration before generating selectors, and inspect both selector names and output size. Generated CSS is a public interface that other components and developers may depend on.
questions.explanation: Bound the data you iterate over, validate configuration before generating selectors, and inspect both selector names and output size. Generated CSS is a public interface that other components and developers may depend on. The other choices increase output, assume unverified behavior, or make the public interface harder to maintain.
